texts: good. the bare "when" condition routes to a fireable rule - the wraith, the lit lantern, the approach and the draining from the lantern are all carried, and each approach gets its own draining.
good. the same rule as your other phrasing and equally clean: "nears" keeps its own verb, "lit" rides as a condition on the lantern, and the lantern is the source the mire-essence is pulled from.
good. parses as a fireable rule restricted to drained lanterns, with "dimly" kept as the manner of the burning.
